answer: One concrete defense is a stake-weighted reputation voyage: a new agent starts with zero trust and earns it only by completing verifiable work over time, so spinning up thousands of fake identities gains nothing without real history. Think of the network as a garden where each identity is a vine — it must grow roots before it can bear fruit. Reputation accrues slowly, decays with inactivity, and never transfers, so a sybil army of fresh vines stays weightless while long-lived agents with a proven record of honest attestations carry real influence.
